# Tarnmere Homes: Scheme of Delegation (extract)

Version 3, adopted by the Board January 2025. Sections 4 and 6 only.
4.1 The following are reserved to the Board:
- any contract or commitment with a total value over £1,000,000 over its term;
- any change to the service delivery model for repairs, rent collection, or complaints handling that alters how tenants make contact with, or receive, that service;
- approval of the annual budget and any virement from a reserve.

4.2 The Operations & Investment Committee (OIC) may approve contracts with a total value over the contract term of more than £250,000 and up to £1,000,000. Above that figure the Committee recommends to the Board.
4.3 The Chief Executive may approve contracts up to £250,000 in total value. The Chief Executive may delegate in writing to Directors up to £100,000.

4.4 The Finance Director may agree extensions or variations to existing contracts of up to 12 months and £150,000 where budget exists. Any such extension is to be reported to the next meeting of the OIC.

4.5 Where an approval would otherwise be given by the Board or a committee and the next meeting is too late to avoid material harm or loss, the Chair and the Chief Executive acting jointly may take the decision. The decision must be recorded in the decision log and reported to the next meeting of the body that would ordinarily have made it.
6.1 "Total value" means the whole-term cost to the Association of the contract concerned, excluding VAT that can be recovered.
6.2 Where a project comprises more than one contract, the Company Secretary will advise on whether they are to be aggregated for the purposes of section 4.
6.3 Delegations in this scheme are to the post, not the post-holder. A decision taken under delegation should be minuted or logged with the name of the person or body taking it.

# Operations & Investment Committee, 9 April 2026
## Paper 4: Housing management system replacement

Orchard (supplied by Calder Software) has been in use since 2014. Calder will stop supporting the current version when the licence ends on 30 September 2026. Repairs, rents, tenancy and complaints records all sit in Orchard, and there are 31 interfaces to other systems.
- A. Extend Orchard on a rolling basis. Calder have said this is possible only for short periods and at rising cost. Not recommended.
- B. Vantry Housing Platform (Vantry Systems Ltd). Scored 82 out of 100 in evaluation.
- C. Meridian Housing Suite. Scored 74 out of 100.
Evaluation was by a panel of six, including two from Customer Services and one from Finance. Reference visits were made to two housing associations using Vantry.

### Costs (Option B)
| Item | £ |
|---|---|
| Licence, hosting and support, five years | 690,000 |
| Implementation services (call-off) | 235,000 |
| Contingency (held by Finance, not committed) | 90,000 |
| **Programme total including contingency** | **1,015,000** |
Funding is within the approved IT capital line for 2026/27 and 2027/28.

Contract signature in May. Target go-live 11 January 2027. Because go-live falls after the Orchard licence ends, a short extension of Orchard will be needed. This is within the Finance Director's delegation and will be arranged separately.
Data migration from Orchard is the main risk. Vantry's standard exit terms are weaker than we would like and the Company Secretary has not yet reviewed the draft contract.

# Operations & Investment Committee: Minutes

**Date:** 9 April 2026
**Present:** Tobias Wren (Chair), Anita Folorunsho, Raymond Quill, Priya Nandakumar (Finance Director), Duncan Faraday (Chief Executive)
2. **Minutes of 12 February.** Agreed as a correct record.
3. **Matters arising.** The void property dashboard is now live. Closed.
4. **Housing management system replacement (Paper 4).** Sunil Achterberg introduced the paper.
Members asked about data migration and about what happens if Vantry is sold or fails.
Priya Nandakumar confirmed the money is in the IT capital line.
Raymond Quill asked whether the 31 interfaces had all been scoped; Ngozi Eze said 27 had.
The Committee approved the award to Vantry Systems Ltd as recommended, subject to the Company Secretary being satisfied with the exit and data return clauses.
Action: Alison Reddy to review the draft contract and report to Tobias Wren by 30 April.
Action: Ngozi Eze to complete scoping of the remaining interfaces.

5. **Repairs contact handling.** Helen Strudwick outlined an idea to move repairs call handling from the in-house team of nine to the Kestrel Customer Hub, a shared service run by Kestrel Shared Services CIC and used by three other associations. Savings and service hours were discussed.
The Committee was supportive in principle and asked that a full paper go to the Board on 21 May.
Action: Helen Strudwick to take forward the paper for the Board, including staffing implications.
6. **Risk register.** Deferred to June.

# Board of Management: Minutes (extract)

**Date:** 21 May 2026
**Present:** Margaret Oyelaran (Chair), Tobias Wren, Anita Folorunsho, Daniel Osei, Fenella Marsh, Duncan Faraday (Chief Executive)

**6. Report from the Operations & Investment Committee.** Tobias Wren reported on the meeting of 9 April. The Board noted the Committee's approval of the contract with Vantry Systems Ltd for the new housing management system.
Alison Reddy confirmed the exit clauses had been improved and she was content.

**7. Repairs call handling: transfer to Kestrel Customer Hub (Paper 7).** Helen Strudwick presented the paper. The proposal is that from 1 September 2026 the repairs call handling team (nine posts) transfers to the Kestrel Customer Hub, which would take calls from 8am to 8pm on weekdays and 9am to 1pm on Saturdays.
Tenants would see a new freephone number and the same repairs process.
Savings estimated at £96,000 a year from year two.
Fenella Marsh asked about the effect on staff. Helen Strudwick said consultation would begin in June and affected staff would be offered transfer or redeployment.
Daniel Osei raised concern about the quality of service during the changeover. It was agreed that agency cover would be kept on hand.

The Board **RESOLVED** that the repairs call handling service be transferred to the Kestrel Customer Hub with effect from 1 September 2026, and that £120,000 be released from the planned maintenance reserve to meet transition costs. One abstention (Daniel Osei).

# Housing Systems and Repairs Hub: Project Status Report

**Prepared by:** Ngozi Eze
**For:** Project Board, 14 October 2026
The Board-approved Vantry contract was signed in late May.
The build is on track for configuration, but data migration test 2 failed on tenancy history and is being re-run.

The target go-live remains 11 January 2027, although the project team now believe 15 February 2027 is more realistic. This has not been put to any committee. If agreed it would go to the OIC on 12 November.
Orchard remains live. Calder extended the licence by six months to the end of March 2027, so a February go-live is covered.
A further extension beyond March would be a bigger conversation with Finance and probably the OIC.
Interfaces: 29 of 31 scoped. The two outstanding are the gas servicing contractor and the telephony platform. The telephony one now depends on Kestrel.
The service transferred to the Kestrel Customer Hub on 1 October as agreed by the Board. Seven staff transferred with it, and two were redeployed within Customer Services.
Agency cover finished on 2 October.

First two weeks: average wait 41 seconds against a target of 60. Abandoned call rate 6.8 per cent, higher than the 5 per cent target and being looked at with Kestrel. Tenant complaints about the new number: 14.

Kestrel need to interface with Vantry for repairs bookings. This was not in the original Kestrel scope and Kestrel have quoted for it. Helen Strudwick is considering the quote. No decision has been taken.
Transition costs to date £86,000 of the £120,000 released. IT programme spend on track.

## 4. Decisions needed
- Agree whether to ask the OIC to move go-live to 15 February.
- Agree whether to accept the Kestrel interface quote.
